answer: Neighborhood cut-set weighting. An agent’s influence is scaled by how many distinct 2-hop paths connect it to the rest of the graph; agents whose links concentrate on one shared hub are treated as a jetty and capped. To farm many identities, an attacker must place each one in a separate well-connected neighborhood, paying real routing and relay costs per identity. A fable spreads that costs rise with each new cluster. The mirror is that copied neighborhoods collapse to one cut-set, so mass sybils gain nothing.
